plan.title: Liver 3-group DE: LRT any-difference + pairwise contrasts
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human liver bulk RNA-seq samples, 4 replicates each in control, treated_a, treated_b, single batch, raw salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples). The research question has two parts that require two distinct tests inside one DESeq2 fit: (1) 'which genes differ across the three groups at all' is answered by the likelihood ratio test (LRT) of the full model ~condition against the reduced model ~1 — this is the ANOVA-like omnibus test, not a pairwise Wald test; (2) 'which genes does each treatment change relative to control' is answered by two named pairwise Wald contrasts, treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control, with control set as the explicit reference level. QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) runs first to confirm the 3 groups separate cleanly and no batch structure or outlier sample confounds the design (the profile states single batch, unpaired, so no blocking term is needed). Low-count pre-filtering keeps genes with >=10 counts in >=4 samples (the smallest group size), leaving independent filtering in the results step to do the rest. Log2 fold changes for the two pairwise contrasts are shrunk with ashr (contrasts between two non-reference levels are not single coefficients, so apeglm does not apply here — both contrasts are in fact against the reference level, but the LRT step already established the omnibus signal via ashr-shrunk stat ranking is used downstream). BH-FDR at 0.05 is applied within each contrast/test, with independent filtering on. Enrichment runs per-contrast (LRT ranked list once, plus the two pairwise Wald contrasts) via fgsea preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome (secondary, filtered to Homo sapiens) using the Wald/LRT statistic as the ranking metric — never the raw fold change or a signed p-value with ties. A single R report step consolidates diagnostics, gene tables (unshrunken + ashr-shrunk LFC), p-value histograms, DE gene counts per contrast, and enrichment results with leading-edge genes, following the reproducibility and reporting rules returned by the knowledge service.
